## Error Handling

| Trigger | Status | Response | Retryable |
|---------|--------|----------|-----------|
| fork already exists | 409 | conflict | False |
| repo limit reached | 409 | conflict | False |
| user blocked by repo owner | 403 | forbidden | False |

### Error Paths

- **org not found** → prepareDoerCreateRepoInOrg → 404
- **no permission to create in org** → prepareDoerCreateRepoInOrg → 403
- **fork already exists or repo limit** → CreateFork → 409
- **user blocked** → CreateFork → 403

## 🛡️ Resiliency

**Risk Level:** high

| Pattern | Status | Severity | Detail |
|---------|--------|----------|--------|
| non_atomic | ❌ missing | high | Multi-step operation: DB insert → git clone → sync branches. If clone fails after DB insert, cleanup runs but could leave partial state if cleanup fails. |
| timeout | ✅ configured | medium | Git clone has 10-minute timeout which is very long for an HTTP request |
| bulkhead | ❌ missing | medium | No limit on concurrent fork operations; many simultaneous forks could exhaust disk I/O |

**Non-atomic operations:**
- ⚠️ DB insert + git clone + branch sync - partial failure leaves cleanup to defer

**Cascading failure risk:** High disk I/O from concurrent forks could slow all git operations

**Graceful degradation:** Cleanup on failure removes partial state
